However the problem that you’d likely run into is that each generation following you would likely lose interest in caring for the vehicle and would either sell it or junk it after an accident or intentional damage. If they engaged in battle they had to win or else their ranks would be routed and their army might even be destroyed. The militaries in this world which can defeat their enemies have their logistics systems intact, well-staffed, and that are well-performing. It’s why the United States last four major wars have been THOUSANDS of miles from our mainland and why none of them were lost due to a lack of supplies and equipment. They were eventually released and they simply disappeared into the general public. Finally a small number remained in France, Belgium, The Netherlands and Germany. A troubled production would likely not secure all of the required financing and things may fall apart during the shoot or at its end and the cast and crew might find themselves paying for their own trips home and filing a grievance with the union or even litigation. Most stunt performers in North America live in and around the Southern California region as that’s where most of the work is, querent. You can choose to live in NYC and work on the television and film productions in that region. However if it’s cheaper to hire stunt performers from Southern California and unless you have specialized skills (See above) you’re unlikely to be hired for productions closer to the West Coast.

Question: When the United States had the military draft, were criminals allowed to serve unlike now?

Judges would routinely tell certain minor offenders that if they joined the US Army or US Marine Corps, they would have their cases dropped, or records sealed. While some did so and were able to turn their lives around, most either blew the judge off; or they got into trouble in the military, and were returned to the civilian world rather quickly. This reached its peak during the Vietnam War when recruitment levels fell, and standards were drastically lowered to fill up the low-skill and dangerous roles in the military. This all came to an end in 1973 when the US military changed over to an all-volunteer force. People who had anything more than minor juvenile or misdemeanor offenses would be refused entry to the service. Judges no longer offered a military “option” to defendants and more stringent requirements for security clearances meant that being unable to pass basic security checks meant that many volunteers got ignored or refused. Although recordkeeping was not a sophisticated as it is today, it can be assumed that the drafts for the Civil War, The Spanish American War and WWI all allowed a number of criminals to serve.

Question: Can the police arrest you on a false allegation if there is no proof?
